title: Bech32 case variants of one address were distinct identities: a member could sign in and vote twice, and an order paying the upper-case form dodged the self-vote rule
A Degent that had voted could vote again after moving to a fresh address (one holder reaching quorum alone)
Concurrent approvals of two orders read the same approvedCount and were assigned the same Degent number
note: rank now from an atomic OrderStore.incrementMeta; also products/degent/services/mint/test/stores.test.ts

title: Concurrent votes decided on the votes read before their own insert, so a quorum reached by simultaneous votes was lost (order stuck in member_review)
Public GET /v1/register/holder/{address} made one ord request per UTXO of any address, and concurrent explorer owner searches repeated thousands of lookups: unbounded upstream amplification

The browser trusted the service for the reveal pubkey, commit address and recipient: a hostile or compromised mint API could lock the payment to its own key (consistent commit address) or pre-sign the child to another address
note: the parent-return-address check in the same fix belongs to the parent path removed by ADR-0010; the key/commit/recipient/content checks stay relevant

title: Per-IP rate limits (mint, market, telegram gate) keyed on the client-supplied left-most X-Forwarded-For hop behind the proxy: any client could bypass them
note: same fix and tests in services/market and services/telegram-gate; Caddy sets X-Client-IP from {client_ip} with trusted_proxies_strict (test/deploy.test.ts)

title: Mint backups were plain gzip written 0644 (recipient addresses, notification e-mails/chat ids, votes, encrypted reveals readable by any host user and in clear off-host); the container's sqlite files were 0644
An order id of '..' became a dot-segment that URL resolution collapsed, sending the order's bearer token to another path
decryptRevealKey used the PBKDF2 iteration count from the recovery bundle unchecked (a bundle re-selected from a file could freeze the tab)
Public read endpoints (/v1/register/*, /v1/explorer, /v1/stats, /v1/orders/{id}) have no per-IP limit; upstream fan-out is now bounded (DGT-SEC-005) but request volume is limited only by the edge
note: internal consumers (telegram gate, market) call the same endpoints, so a per-IP GET limit needs an allowlist or edge rules

title: Every upload of a fresh order triggers a paid vision art review; cost is bounded only by the per-IP POST limit
Recovery passphrase minimum is 8 characters; a stolen bundle can be brute-forced offline (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000 iterations)

The recovery bundle's AAD binds the order id and reveal pubkey, not the rescue parameters (recipient, commit): whoever can edit the user's bundle file can redirect an offline rescue (with the service up, parameters are compared with the service's)
The order token and the encrypted K_e live in localStorage; any script running on the origin can read them
note: CSP script-src 'self' (no inline script), frame-ancestors 'none'; K_e stays encrypted under the passphrase

title: CSP allows style-src 'unsafe-inline' (React style attributes)
note: scripts are 'self' only; CSS injection cannot run code

title: Two buy sessions for one listing can both be broadcast (the listing is claimed after broadcast); only one can confirm and no funds are lost, but the loser sees a failed purchase
buyPrepare makes one ord request per buyer UTXO (safeUtxos) with no cap
One Degent can admit several Telegram accounts in turn (verify, move the Degent, verify again) until the next re-verification run
note: re-verification kicks every account whose wallet no longer holds a Degent; one wallet <-> one active account

title: GitHub Actions are pinned by tag, not commit SHA
GET /v1/orders/{id} is public and shows the recipient address and timeline
note: order ids carry 96 random bits; the recipient is public on chain after reveal

title: Order notification subscriptions can target any e-mail address or Telegram chat (max 3 per order, order token required)
Content uploads (up to 4 MiB) are buffered in memory per request
note: the order token is checked before the body is read; POST/PUT are rate limited per client

title: A revealing order that times out releases the parent lease while its fully signed parent reveal may still propagate; the next reveal can conflict on the parent until one confirms

ANYONECANPAY leaves the parent input's value unsigned by the user: a compromised service could attach a smaller parent UTXO so the child's first sat lands in output 0 (the collection address); only the policy signer guards it
The policy signer checks input 1's hash-type byte but not its signature, not nLockTime/nSequence/version, and computes the fee rate from the quoted weight
No KMS/HSM policy signer: mainnet cannot start, and signet keeps the parent key in a plaintext file
@bsh/identity decodeAddress/verifySignIn accept upper-case bech32 (the comment says lower-case only), so SIWB sessions are not canonical identities for consumers
note: degent canonicalises itself since DGT-SEC-001; fix in DegentClub/scribbit, then bump the pin

title: @bsh/identity InMemoryNonceStore sweeps expired nonces with the wall clock while verifySignIn uses the injected clock: with a skewed or injected clock, concurrent challenges invalidate each other
@bsh/identity verifySignIn accepts legacy signmessage signatures by default (the mint and the gate use the default; the market disables them)
